newsitem.title: GREECE: SEAMEN'S STRIKE LEAVE SHIPS TIED AT GREEK PORTS.
newsitem.headline: SEAMEN'S STRIKE LEAVE SHIPS TIED AT GREEK PORTS.

text.p: Striking Greek seamen jumped into the water to prevent ships from docking at two ports on Thursday during a nationwide walkout that has kept most commericial and passenger vessels from sailing for four days.

Police said there were minor clashes at the ports of Piraeus and Rethymno on the island of Crete between stranded passengers, lorry drivers and seamen who are on strike for the fourth day to press for better insurance, pension and tax benefits.
They said no one was hurt but very few ships managed to depart. A Piraeus Port Authority telephone recording informed callers that no ships were sailing because of the strike.
Talks between the Panhellenic Seamen's Federation (PNO) and merchant marine ministry officials on Thursday were unsuccessful, union representatives said.
"Our principal concern is the unemployment problem. Next we are worried about pensions and insurance schemes," PNO representative Giorgos Ilamakis told Reuters.
He said union leaders tried but failed to meet Merchant Marine Minister Stavros Soumakis after a protest march to the ministry.
The four-day strike which affects all ships with Greek crews will end at 0400 GMT on Friday. PNO is considering extending the walkout if its demands are not met.
Owners of passenger ships have tried to declare the strike illegal and a court decision is expected later on Thursday, the Union of Coastal Passenger Ships' Owners said in a statement.

"If the court hearing declares the strike illegal, then all seamen will be forced to return to their jobs," said Constantinos Tatakis, a lawyer for the shipowners. --Margarita Sotiropoulou, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
